executiveSummary: Analysis of 20 surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO spanning November 2025 through May 2026 identifies multiple concurrent threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1), a BSL-3 select agent, is flagged across two PAHO updates indicating sustained zoonotic activity in the Americas region with pandemic spillover risk. Additional high-priority signals include mpox circulation in the Americas, yellow fever activity, and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome. Simultaneously, resurgent measles, pertussis, and dengue amplify pressure on regional health systems already managing seasonal influenza transitions in both hemispheres.
bottomLine: The Americas face a complex multi-pathogen threat landscape anchored by sustained H5N1 zoonotic activity and compounded by resurgent vaccine-preventable diseases and arboviral surges.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Two PAHO epidemiological updates issued within four months (November 2025, March 2026) indicating sustained regional activity
Zoonotic spillover risk to humans from animal reservoirs; BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential
Ongoing animal-sector detections prompting repeated regional alerts
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interfaces; reinforce PPE protocols for agricultural and veterinary workers; expedite antiviral stockpile assessments and pandemic preparedness planning

threats.name: Mpox
signals: Dedicated PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 indicating active regional transmission
Continued community spread following 2022-2024 global outbreak trajectory
BSL-3 pathogen requiring heightened containment and contact tracing
threats.action: Strengthen case detection and contact tracing networks; ensure vaccine availability (MVA-BN/JYNNEOS) for high-risk populations; enforce BSL-3 laboratory protocols for specimen handling

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating active epizootics or human cases
Yellow fever is a BSL-3 select agent with high case fatality rate in unvaccinated individuals
Seasonal risk elevation in tropical zones of South America
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in at-risk populations; deploy rapid diagnostics to affected areas; coordinate vector control and primate surveillance with national health authorities

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO update in February 2026 amid historically high dengue burden following record 2024 season
Risk of severe dengue and DHF in hyperendemic countries
Multiple serotype co-circulation increasing risk of severe disease
threats.action: Scale up integrated vector management; enhance hospital surge capacity for severe dengue; promote community-level vector source reduction campaigns

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 signaling resurgence in region that achieved elimination
Vaccination coverage gaps post-COVID-19 pandemic creating susceptible cohorts
High transmission potential (R0 12-18) in under-immunized communities
threats.action: Conduct urgent vaccination coverage assessments; launch supplementary immunization activities in low-coverage areas; reinforce measles IgM surveillance at health facilities

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two PAHO updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained and increasing transmission
Cyclical resurgence pattern consistent with waning immunity and vaccine hesitancy trends
Risk concentrated in infants too young to be fully vaccinated
threats.action: Reinforce maternal Tdap vaccination programs; strengthen infant immunization schedules; enhance laboratory confirmation capacity to distinguish from other respiratory pathogens

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued December 2025 indicating cases across multiple American countries
High case fatality rate (30-40%) with no licensed vaccine or specific antiviral
Person-to-person transmission possible for Andes virus variant
threats.action: Strengthen rodent exposure risk communication; enhance clinical recognition and early ICU referral protocols; investigate potential Andes virus person-to-person clusters

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and RSV Co-circulation
threats.pathogen: Influenza A/B viruses; Respiratory Syncytial Virus
signals: PAHO alerts for simultaneous influenza-RSV co-circulation in January 2026 and start of Southern Hemisphere season in April 2026
Dual epidemic peaks risk overwhelming pediatric and elderly care capacity
Northern Hemisphere 2025-26 season transition documented in December 2025 alert
threats.action: Promote influenza vaccination uptake ahead of respective hemispheric seasons; prepare healthcare surge protocols for dual respiratory epidemic scenarios; monitor RSV severity in high-risk pediatric groups

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents were identified in this surveillance cycle. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) generated the highest concern, with two PAHO updates (November 2025 and March 2026) documenting sustained zoonotic activity across the Americas, representing ongoing pandemic spillover risk. Yellow fever virus, also a BSL-3 agent, prompted a PAHO epidemiological alert in March 2026 indicating active risk in tropical Americas. Mpox virus (Orthopoxvirus, BSL-3) was the subject of an April 2026 PAHO update confirming continued regional circulation. All three pathogens require strict containment protocols, and H5N1 in particular warrants pandemic preparedness escalation given its animal reservoir dynamics.

diseases: ECDC Communicable Disease Threats (Weeks 16-20 2026 - multiple pathogens monitored)

amrSignals: No explicit AMR-specific reports identified in this surveillance batch; Bordetella pertussis macrolide resistance warrants monitoring given resurgent pertussis activity
Influenza antiviral resistance (oseltamivir) surveillance should be integrated into H5N1 monitoring protocols given therapeutic reliance on neuraminidase inhibitors
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous resurgence of multiple vaccine-preventable diseases (measles, pertussis) suggests systemic immunization coverage erosion across the Americas, likely a legacy of COVID-19 pandemic disruptions
Repeated H5N1 alerts across consecutive months indicate expanding or persistent animal reservoir activity rather than isolated spillover events, elevating pandemic preparedness urgency
Southern Hemisphere influenza season onset (April 2026) overlapping with ongoing RSV and dengue transmission creates compounded respiratory and arboviral burden in tropical South American countries
Chikungunya alert in February 2026 alongside dengue activity suggests expanding Aedes mosquito vector pressure, potentially linked to climate-driven range expansion
GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert from PAHO (February 2026) signals an emerging public health concern around counterfeit or off-label pharmaceutical products in the Americas
